description:
gh:#46 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/46 — carries the full step-by-step. Child of the MGXS work op-84bc / gh:#42.

CORRECTION TO op-84bc FIRST. That bead says 'there are no MGXS tallies'. WRONG, and I should not have written it. outram-mc-libs/src/tally/ already has: ScoreType {Flux, Total, Fission, Absorption, NuFission, KappaFission, ScatterN, Current, Events}; filters {CellFilter, MaterialFilter, EnergyFilter, UniverseFilter, MeshFilter, SpatialLegendreFilter}; RegularMesh with get_bin(Position); TallyBin with sum, sum-of-squares, mean and rel_std_dev. Energy grouping, spatial binning and every reaction rate MGXS needs are present.

THE REAL GAPS ARE NARROWER AND SHARPER:
  1. NO SCATTER MATRIX. ScoreType::ScatterN is (n,xn) scatter — a scalar, not group-to-group. Sigma_s(g->g') is the one MGXS quantity with no score behind it, and the one a multigroup solver cannot run without.
  2. RegularMesh is the ONLY mesh. Axis-aligned structured only, so constants cannot land on the mesh the deterministic solver actually uses.
  3. No collapse, no bridge — as op-84bc says.

PATH A, CSG BINNING (first, no new geometry work). A1 add a ScatterMatrix score, n_groups x n_groups bins per spatial bin, scored at each scattering event from pre/post-collision energies already in the transport loop — the only genuinely new physics plumbing in the seam. A2 build the standard tally set (Flux, Absorption, NuFission, KappaFission, Total, plus A1) under EnergyFilter x MaterialFilter/CellFilter. A3 flux-weighted collapse, Sigma_x,g = R_x,g / phi_g, chi from the fission-neutron production spectrum, gated on Mgxs::consistency_residual. A4 bridge to GroupConstants — D = 1/(3 Sigma_tr), removal = absorption + out-scatter (A1 row sum less the diagonal), chi split prompt/delayed, DOCUMENTING the diffusion-coefficient convention. A5 verify: k-eff three ways on one geometry (CE MC, run_keff_mg on the collapsed library, genfoam diffusion on the bridged constants).

PATH B, TET / POLYHEDRAL-DUAL MESH BINNING. Why: genfoam marches on an FvMesh, so constants should land PER FV CELL, not per CSG zone — a homogenised zone constant throws away the detail the deterministic solver exists to resolve.
  B1 POINT LOCATION ON FvMesh. It does not exist today; Geometry::locate is CSG-only. This is the load-bearing piece. Tets: barycentric, exact and cheap. Polyhedral duals (what poly_dual_mesh produces) are non-convex in general — decompose each into face-apex tets ONCE at load and store it, then it reduces to the tet case. Needs a BVH/octree over cell bounding boxes; check whether stochastic/spatial_index.rs generalises before writing a second one.
  B2 UnstructuredMeshFilter, same shape as MeshFilter but delegating to B1. The tally side needs no other change — which is why B1 is the whole difficulty.
  B3 COST CONTROL. A location query per collision on a million-cell mesh is the obvious way to make this unusably slow. Track-length with segment splitting (more accurate, more queries) vs collision estimator (one query per collision, noisier in optically thin cells) — measure, do not assume. State cells, particles and a wall-clock ceiling.
  B4 STATISTICS PER CELL. Far more bins means far fewer events per bin. A rel_std_dev gate must REFUSE to emit an unconverged constant rather than passing noise downstream — a noisy Sigma_r in one cell produces a plausible-looking flux shape that is wrong. Correctness requirement, not a nicety.
  B5 verify as A5, plus mesh refinement: coarse and refined collapses must give the same k-eff within statistics, else the binning or estimator is wrong.

ORDERING: A BEFORE B, WITHOUT EXCEPTION. A shares A1/A3/A4/A5 with B; only the binning differs. B first means debugging a new scatter score, a new collapse, a new bridge AND a new point-location routine at once, with a three-way k-eff disagreement and no way to localise it. poly_dual_mesh already exists in outram-foam-cli/src/bin, so B's test meshes can be generated in-tree.

NOT IN SCOPE: transport physics beyond the scatter score. Self-shielding and URR are op-cpz, which validates the collapse against a real NJOY GENDF golden tape — a STRONGER check than A5 because it is external rather than self-referential. Sequence op-cpz alongside A3/A4, not after.

Related: op-84bc / gh:#42, op-wpi0 / gh:#43, op-cpz.
title: MGXS seam step by step: CSG binning, then tet/polyhedral-dual mesh binning

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: 2026-07-10 DONE: all per-fluid hardcoded transport complete. Added friction-theory viscosity (methane/H2S/SF6/n-pentane), kinetic-theory (R125), powers_of_Tr + collision_integral_powers_of_Tstar dilute, empirical initial density, methanol viscosity (Chung-style), methane conductivity (full critical region), and the ammonia/R123 critical-conductivity terms. description: MAINTAINER DECISION. The workspace now has two overlapping surface-to-volume meshers with two DIFFERENT dual algorithms: outram-foam-mesh (blockMesh, snappyHexMesh castellation, cell-centre polyDualMesh -- measured exactly orthogonal on a uniform block, 1e-12) and outram-park-fork-cfmesh (Cartesian/tet/polyhedral pipeline with a median/Donald vertex-centred dual -- orthogonality UNMEASURED). Both crates' docs now document the split honestly (2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass added a side-by-side table to cfmesh's README), but nothing resolves it. Two duals with different quality characteristics is a maintenance and user-confusion risk: a user picking by crate name cannot know one dual is measured-exact and the other unmeasured. Decide: converge on one dual implementation, keep both with a documented use-case split, or make cfmesh consume outram-foam-mesh's dual. Related: op-cyo, and the cfmesh false claim (now fixed) that no other unstructured mesher existed in the workspace.
title: DECISION: converge or formally split outram-foam-mesh vs outram-park-fork-cfmesh

description:
**Numerical differentiation** on the hybrid backend.

Note the distinction up front, because the crate already has one of these:
`src/fv_operators/` implements *spatial* FV gradient/divergence/laplacian over
a mesh. This bead is about **general-purpose numerical differentiation of a
supplied function** — the derivative and Jacobian machinery that root finders,
Rosenbrock ODE integrators, and sensitivity work need. Do not duplicate the FV
operators; cross-reference them in the docs so a reader knows which is which.

What to deliver:

- Finite differences: forward, backward, central, and a Richardson-extrapolated
  variant, with a documented step-size rule (the `sqrt(eps) * scale` trade-off
  between truncation and round-off error) rather than a hard-coded `h`.
- **Batched derivative evaluation** — N independent points, the GPU-worthy
  shape.
- **Jacobian assembly** for an N-dimensional function: N+1 (forward) or 2N
  (central) evaluations, all independent, which is the genuinely useful
  parallel win here and the direct feeder for `rosenbrock23` and for
  multi-dimensional Newton in the root-finding bead.
- Optional, only if it stays simple: forward-mode dual-number autodiff as an
  exact alternative to finite differences for functions written in-crate. If it
  starts pulling in a dependency or generic machinery that raises the reader's
  context load, drop it — the human-interface-layer rule outranks the
  convenience.
- **`uom` care**: a derivative changes dimension (`d(enthalpy)/d(temperature)`
  is a heat capacity). Do not solve this by dropping to raw `f64` in the public
  signature. If the generic form cannot be typed cleanly, prefer a small number
  of concrete typed wrappers over a generic one nobody can read.

V&V: analytic derivatives of smooth test functions; verify the observed
convergence order versus `h` matches theory (1st order forward, 2nd central)
and that the round-off floor appears where the step-size rule predicts. Record
the measured numbers.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: numerical differentiation on the hybrid backend (finite differences + batched Jacobians)

description:
Flagged 2026-08-13 by maintainer instruction ('LMTD as last resort, but flag this for future correction').

MEASURED: given the plant's OWN boundary conditions and its calibrated STEAM_GENERATOR_UA_W_PER_K, the zoned-LMTD
remedy's steady solve returns
    duty          9.36 MW   vs 10 MWth        (-6.4%)
    steam outlet  366.2 degC vs published 440 (-73.8 K)
    helium return +30.9 K
So engaging this remedy visibly moves the plant by TENS OF KELVIN -- an order of magnitude more than any other
approximation in htgr_sim_v1 (the substep reduction, by comparison, costs +5.24 K).

CAUSE, understood not guessed: STEAM_GENERATOR_UA_W_PER_K was calibrated against a COUPLED TRANSIENT WITH FEEDWATER
FEEDBACK, not against a fixed-boundary steady solve. A steady solve at that UA therefore does not reproduce the
operating point. This is not a defect in the zoning or the LMTD algebra -- both were verified (duty residual exactly
0, conductance residual 1.540e-12, LMTD and eps-NTU agreeing to 1.332e-12 at C_r -> 0).

FIX OPTIONS: calibrate a separate steady UA for this path, or reconcile the two calibrations so one UA serves both.
The second is preferable but may not be achievable -- the transient calibration has feedwater feedback in the loop
and the steady one does not, so they are not obliged to agree.

UNTIL FIXED: LMTD is the last-resort remedy only, behind Bedok, and any state it produces is indicative only. The
variant's doc comment carries this warning.

Related: op-3lay (the remedy programme), and the note that Bedok is the preferred corrector -- it is verified against
a closed-form eps-NTU reference to 0.086% of span and does not have this problem.
title: LMTD cross remedy: the steady state it imposes is not the plant's operating point (-73.8 K on steam outlet)
